- Next I am reading that task file and checking the worktree to determine whether this turn is planning-only or execution.

- Read the reduce-loop task file; it points to plan 32-collapse-operator-config-parser-boundary.md.
- The worktree is currently only dirty from Ralph bookkeeping files plus an untracked regenerated .ralph/current_task.txt.
- Next I am reading the referenced plan and the improve-code-boundaries skill instructions to determine whether I should execute or switch the plan back to verification.

- The operator duplication is real: parser/private_schema owns raw operator input structs and load_config maps them into OperatorConfigV2.
- I am now reading the exact operator struct definitions, loader branch, and operator TOML test renderers to identify the smallest canonical shape that can replace the raw wrapper layer.
- The goal for this slice is to reuse existing runtime operator types and delete mapping-only structs/helpers rather than move them.

- Replaced RuntimeDocument.pgtm with a raw TOML subtree and removed the top-level parser wrapper structs for operator documents from private_schema.rs.
- Moved operator parsing onto a single shared loader path in load_config.rs and rewired operator test/runtime TOML builders to construct TOML values directly from the surviving leaf input types.
- Running formatter and searching for any remaining references before compiling or running the required checks.

- cargo fmt and make check both passed after the operator boundary collapse.
- I am validating the explicit make lint step and checking the line-diff script to make sure this slice actually reduced code rather than just moved it around.
- If the reduction is real, I will continue through make test and make test-long before doing task bookkeeping.

- make test-long failed in the Docker release build because private_schema.rs kept an unconditional PgtmApiTransportExpectation import after the refactor.
- I fixed the import by gating it to test/internal-test-support only; this was a real release-profile regression surfaced only by the ultra-long setup image build.
- After formatting, I need to rerun make check, make lint, make test, and make test-long from the final tree state before any bookkeeping.

- Final validation is blocked only by one HA ultra-long failure: ha_rejoin_and_restart_recovery::blocked_basebackup_recovery_recovers_after_unblock.
- The symptom is that node-a exits during the scenario and the status probe later reports no published 8443/tcp port for that container.
- Next I am reading the failing run artifacts and rendered configs/logs to determine whether the operator config builder regression caused the crash.

- The failing HA scenario appears to stem from runtime startup resolving pgtm operator auth secrets even though startup only needs the advertised operator API route.
- I changed runtime pgtm parsing to skip operator auth secret reads while leaving full operator config loads unchanged, and added a regression test for unreadable operator auth token files in runtime configs.
- Next I am running focused unit and HA scenario checks before rerunning the full required validation set.

- Focused regression checks passed, but the first full rerun of make check failed on a clippy lint in the new unreadable-token regression test.
- I fixed the lint by precomputing the TOML string instead of calling display().to_string() inside format! arguments.
- After formatting, I need to rerun the full required gate set again from this final tree.

- Final validation passed from the final tree: make check, make lint, make test, and make test-long all succeeded.
- The key fix after the operator boundary collapse was to stop runtime startup from resolving pgtm operator auth secrets that it never uses; this also has a regression test and the previously failing blocked-basebackup HA scenario now passes.
- Next I am checking the current line totals and then doing Ralph bookkeeping, task switch, commit, and push while keeping passes false if the global 19k target is still not met.
